items.title: Lookahead Bias Must Be Blocked Before Backtest Conclusions

applies_when: A strategy evaluation uses historical data to estimate future performance.
Features, labels, fills, or filters may accidentally include information unavailable at decision time.
not_applicable_when: The task is only documenting a known historical event and not using it for predictive evaluation.

content.statement: A backtest is not credible until lookahead paths are checked and blocked for features, labels, fills, and filters.
content.rationale: Using information that was not available at the simulated decision time can make performance appear better than it would have been in live use.
procedure: Identify the decision timestamp for every signal.
Check that every feature is computed only from data available before or at that timestamp.
Check labels and future returns are not joined back into feature rows.
Check fill logic does not use future candle extremes without a deterministic assumption.
examples: A next-bar return column must not be available as an input feature.
anti_patterns: Merging future labels into the feature frame before train/test splitting.
Using full-candle high/low to prove an intrabar entry without an explicit fill model.
validation: Review joins between labels and features.
risk_notes: Lookahead bias can survive high-level metric review and must be checked at data lineage level.
content.citation_notes: This sample uses CEK-TA internal schema as an example source; replace with public/primary sources before broad professional approval.

assumptions: No additional assumptions identified beyond the stated backtest setting.

items.title: Same-Candle TP/SL Requires Explicit Fill Ordering

metadata.tree_path: CEK-TA / Trading Engineering / Replay And Simulation / Fill Model

applies_when: A candle's high and low both cross take-profit and stop-loss levels.
The available data does not reveal intrabar event order.
not_applicable_when: Tick, trade, or order-book replay data provides deterministic event ordering.

content.statement: When TP and SL are both touched inside the same candle, a backtest or simulator must use an explicit deterministic fill-order rule and report that assumption.
content.rationale: OHLC candles do not encode the sequence of intrabar prices, so assuming a favorable order can overstate performance.
procedure: Detect candles where both TP and SL are reachable.
Apply the configured deterministic ordering rule.
Report how many trades depend on same-candle ordering.
Run sensitivity checks under conservative and optimistic ordering if needed.
examples: A conservative model may choose stop-first when sequence is unknown.
anti_patterns: Always choosing TP first without documenting the assumption.
validation: Compare metrics under alternate fill-order policies.
risk_notes: This rule is assumption-sensitive and should not be merged with tick-data execution rules.
content.citation_notes: This sample is based on CEK-TA fill model contract and should gain external sources in Phase 17.

assumptions: Only OHLC/K-line data is available for the ambiguous candle.

source_evidence.evidence_summary: The CEK-TA fill model spec requires deterministic assumptions for ambiguous fill ordering.

limitations: Example item requires external source support before broad professional approval.

conflicts.resolution: This item applies to OHLC/K-line ambiguity; tick replay with event ordering belongs to a different scope.
conflicts.applicability_boundary: Use only when intrabar sequence is unavailable.

items.title: External Project Adapter Must Keep CEK-TA Tooling Read-Only By Default

applies_when: A business project uses CEK-TA through AGENTS.md, Project Adapter, Skills, MCP, or contribution templates.
not_applicable_when: A separate approved task card explicitly grants a narrower write permission.

content.statement: External projects must treat CEK-TA MCP/RAG tools as read-only by default and submit reusable experience only through proposed contribution files.
content.rationale: CEK-TA is a support layer; it must not read secrets, place trades, or write approved knowledge from a business project context.
procedure: Declare allowed_cek_ta_tools and blocked_cek_ta_tools in the Project Adapter.
examples: search_expert_knowledge is allowed; write_approved_knowledge is blocked.
anti_patterns: Letting an external project directly edit CEK-TA approved knowledge.
validation: Check contribution initial status is proposed.
risk_notes: Permission creep can leak project-private data or pollute reusable knowledge.
content.citation_notes: Based on CEK-TA Phase 10 runtime integration templates.

assumptions: External project has not been separately granted write permission.
